the_problem: StoreDot failed to complete a planned private fundraising round of USD 30-50 million that its USD 800M SPAC merger with Andretti Acquisition Corp. II required as a minimum cash injection; institutional investors did not commit and SPAC redemptions were expected to be high, which would have left too little cash after listing. It had raised about USD 200M and was valued at USD 1.5B in its 2022 Series D.
the_decision: CEO and co-founder Doron Myersdorf and Andretti mutually cancelled the USD 800M SPAC deal rather than list with insufficient cash. Myersdorf told Calcalist the company would now raise "several tens of millions of dollars" independently, blaming global automotive uncertainty for tightening financing, and said he believes StoreDot can raise it and avoid liquidation. About a month earlier the company had laid off most of its employees.
the_outcome: USD 800M SPAC deal collapsed (19 Feb 2026, planned Q2 2026 close); Herzliya headcount cut to a few dozen; company in a cash crunch with liquidation risk, down from a USD 1.5B 2022 valuation.
